lessons.title: Kinds of film
lessons.scenario: Omar and Lily talk with Smarty about different kinds of film they like or dislike.

items.example: We watched a comedy last night.
items.note: Use ‘a comedy’ for a happy film that makes people smile and laugh.

items.example: I do not watch a horror film at night.
items.note: Say ‘a horror film’ for a dark, frightening film.

items.example: My little brother loves a cartoon.
items.note: Use ‘a cartoon’ for a film made with drawings or computer art.

items.note: Say ‘an action film’ for a film with running, jumping, and big adventures.

items.example: I watched a documentary about birds.
items.note: Use ‘a documentary’ for a film about real life, animals, or history.

items.example: I dislike horror films.
items.note: Say ‘I dislike’ as a polite way to say you do not like something.

grammar.title: a vs. an with film types
grammar.explanation: Use ‘an’ before a vowel sound, as in ‘an action film’, and ‘a’ before a consonant sound, as in ‘a comedy’ or ‘a cartoon’.

lessons.title: Comparing
lessons.scenario: Tom and Mia compare two films and two screens with Smarty.

items.example: This song is better than the first song.
items.note: Use ‘better’ when one thing is more good than another.

items.example: The second film was worse than the book.
items.note: Say ‘worse’ when one thing is less good than another.

items.example: The cinema screen is bigger than my TV.
items.note: Use ‘bigger than’ to compare the size of two things.

items.example: An action film is more exciting than a documentary.
items.note: Say ‘more exciting’ when something gives you stronger energy and interest.

items.example: A comedy is funnier than a horror film.
items.note: Use ‘funnier’ when something makes you laugh more.

items.example: This band is much better than that band.
items.note: Say ‘much better’ when one thing is a lot better than another.

grammar.title: Comparing two things
grammar.explanation: Add ‘-er’ to short words (big → bigger, funny → funnier) and use ‘more’ with longer words (more exciting). ‘Better’ and ‘worse’ are special forms. Use ‘than’ before the second thing.
examples: A cinema screen is bigger than a phone screen.
This comedy is funnier than that cartoon.

practice.prompt: You like the new film more than the old film. The new film is ___.
practice.explanation: ‘Better’ means higher quality or nicer than the other.

practice.prompt: Which word is the opposite of ‘better’?
practice.explanation: ‘Worse’ is the opposite of ‘better’.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.

A comedy is funnier than a documentary.
A horror film is worse than a documentary.
practice.explanation: Smarty compared an action film and a documentary using ‘more exciting’.

practice.prompt: Match each comparison with its meaning.
practice.explanation: ‘Bigger than’ compares size, ‘funnier’ compares humour, and ‘much better’ shows a big difference.

lessons.title: The best

items.example: This is the best song on the album.
items.note: Use ‘the best’ for number one out of everything.

grammar.title: Superlatives: the best, the most...
grammar.explanation: Use ‘the’ + ‘-est’ for short adjectives (funny → the funniest) and ‘the most’ for longer adjectives (the most popular). ‘The best’ and ‘the worst’ are special forms.
examples: This is the most popular band.

mission.setup: Tell Smarty about the best and worst films or songs you know.

turns.smarty: What is your all-time favourite: a comedy, an action film, or a cartoon?
accept: ^(?:a comedy|an action film|a cartoon|a documentary)(?: is my alltime favourite| is my all time favourite)?$
^my alltime favourite is (?:a comedy|an action film|a cartoon|a documentary)$
^my all time favourite is (?:a comedy|an action film|a cartoon|a documentary)$
turns.example: A comedy is my all-time favourite.
turns.hint: Use ‘my all-time favourite’ in your sentence.

turns.smarty: Which instrument makes the best music: the piano, the guitar, or the violin?
accept: ^(?:the )?(?:piano|guitar|violin)(?: makes the best music| is the best)?$

turns.smarty: Is there a kind of film you hate?
accept: ^i hate (?:horror films|a horror film|action films|an action film|comedies|a comedy|cartoons|a cartoon|documentaries|a documentary|boring films)$

lessons.title: Review
lessons.scenario: Smarty hosts a film and music quiz with Ana and Leo.

practice.prompt: Which film shows real animals or real history?
practice.explanation: A documentary is about real life.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: A comedy is funnier than an action film.
practice.answer: A comedy is funnier than an action film.
options: A comedy is funnier than an action film.
An action film is worse than a comedy.
A cartoon is bigger than a comedy.
practice.explanation: Smarty compared a comedy and an action film with ‘funnier’.

practice.prompt: Match the opposites.
practice.explanation: ‘Better’/‘worse’, ‘the best’/‘the worst’, and ‘I enjoy’/‘I dislike’ are pairs of opposites.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
practice.answer: This is the most popular cartoon.
practice.explanation: ‘The most popular’ comes before ‘cartoon’.

practice.prompt: Complete the comparison.
practice.text: This concert is ___ than last year.
practice.explanation: Use ‘more exciting’ with ‘than’ when comparing two concerts.

practice.prompt: Compare the two instruments. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: A piano is ___ a flute.
practice.explanation: A piano is much larger in size, so it is ‘bigger than’ a flute.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: The new singer is ___ than the old singer.
practice.explanation: Use ‘much better’ before ‘than’.

practice.prompt: Say this sentence aloud.
practice.text: I hate boring documentaries, but I love comedies.
practice.answer: I hate boring documentaries, but I love comedies.
practice.explanation: Great contrast using ‘I hate’ and ‘I love’!

turns.smarty: Which is better: a cartoon or a documentary?
accept: ^(?:a cartoon|a documentary)(?: is (?:much )?better(?: than (?:a cartoon|a documentary))?)?$

lessons.title: Feelings
lessons.scenario: Mia, Omar, and Smarty talk about how films and concerts make them feel.

items.example: I was bored because the film was long.
items.note: Say ‘bored’ to describe how you feel when nothing is interesting.

image.describe: a sleepy kitten resting its chin on a paw looking unimpressed during a slow show

items.example: We are excited about the concert tonight.
items.note: Use ‘excited’ when you feel happy and full of energy about something.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat jumping with joy and sparkling eyes holding two concert tickets

items.example: Omar was scared during the horror film.
items.note: Say ‘scared’ when you feel afraid or frightened.

image.describe: a wide-eyed kitten peeking out from behind a sofa pillow in a dark room

items.example: I was surprised by the end of the film.
items.note: Use ‘surprised’ when something unexpected happens.

image.describe: a cat with raised ears and wide eyes opening a gift box with musical notes

items.example: The singer and the band were amazing!
items.note: Say ‘amazing’ when a film, song, or show is wonderfully good.

image.describe: a dazzling concert stage with golden stars and a cheering crowd of cats

items.example: I am into action films and rock music.
items.note: Say ‘I am into’ to talk about a hobby, music, or film type you enjoy a lot.

grammar.title: -ed and -ing adjectives
grammar.explanation: Words ending in ‘-ed’ (bored, excited, scared, surprised) describe how a person feels. Words ending in ‘-ing’ (boring, exciting, amazing) describe the film, song, or thing.
examples: I am bored because the film is boring.
We are excited because the concert is amazing.

practice.prompt: How do people often feel during a horror film?
practice.explanation: Horror films are frightening, so people feel ‘scared’.

practice.prompt: The documentary was boring, so Mia felt ___.
practice.explanation: Use ‘bored’ (-ed) for how a person feels, and ‘boring’ (-ing) for the film.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I am excited because the band is amazing.
practice.answer: I am excited because the band is amazing.
options: I am excited because the band is amazing.
I am bored because the band is boring.
I am scared because the film is old.
practice.explanation: Smarty felt ‘excited’ and called the band ‘amazing’.

practice.prompt: Match the situation with the feeling.
practice.explanation: You feel scared in a horror film, excited at a concert, and bored in a boring film.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order to say what films you like a lot.
practice.answer: I am into comedies and cartoons.
practice.explanation: Use ‘I am into’ followed by the things you enjoy.

practice.prompt: Nobody expected the ending! Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Everyone was ___ at the end of the film.
practice.explanation: Use ‘surprised’ when something unexpected happens.

practice.prompt: Describe the concert, not the person. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: The concert yesterday was ___!
practice.explanation: Use ‘amazing’ (-ing) to describe the concert.

practice.prompt: Describe how Sam feels before the show. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Sam is ___ because the action film is starting.
practice.explanation: Use ‘excited’ (-ed) to describe how Sam feels.

practice.prompt: Say this sentence aloud.
practice.text: I am into music and amazing films.
practice.answer: I am into music and amazing films.
practice.explanation: Well done! ‘I am into’ sounds very natural.

questions.explanation: Smarty says: Now I am into documentaries about music too!

lessons.title: Going out
lessons.canDo: Buy tickets and choose a film
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Ben buy tickets at the cinema, choose a film, and share their opinions afterwards.

items.example: Two tickets please, for the comedy.
items.note: Say ‘Two tickets please’ at the cinema or concert when you buy two seats.

items.example: What time does it start? At seven o'clock.
items.note: Ask ‘What time does it start?’ to check when a film or concert begins.

items.example: I enjoyed the film. It was great!
items.note: Say ‘It was great’ after a film or concert to say you loved it.

practice.prompt: You and your friend arrive at the cinema. What do you say to buy seats?
practice.explanation: Say ‘Two tickets please’ to buy two tickets.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Smarty asked ‘What time does it start?’ to check the film time.

practice.prompt: Match the phrases with when you say them.
practice.explanation: You buy tickets first, ask the start time, and say ‘It was great’ afterwards.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order after an amazing concert.
practice.explanation: ‘It was great’ gives a happy opinion about the show.

practice.prompt: Test your Unit 5 vocabulary! Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Mia plays the ___ and Sam plays the drum.
practice.explanation: A violin is a musical instrument, like a drum.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about film types.
practice.text: I dislike horror films, so ___ a comedy.
practice.explanation: Use ‘I prefer’ to say what you choose instead.

practice.prompt: Compare the cinema screen and a computer screen.
practice.text: The cinema screen is ___ a computer screen.
practice.explanation: Use ‘bigger than’ when comparing two sizes.

practice.prompt: Complete the superlative sentence.

practice.explanation: Use ‘the best’ when comparing one band to all others.

practice.prompt: Describe how you felt during the exciting action film.

practice.explanation: Use ‘excited’ (-ed) for your feeling.

practice.answer: Two tickets please. What time does it start?
